zh: 中央大学（🇯🇵），简称中央（ちゅうおう）、中大（ちゅうだい），是一所总校位于东京都八王子市东中野的日本私立大学. 其前身为1885年7月成立的，1920年合并其他学校成立. 该校以法律见长，毕业生司法官考试及律师考试及格率为日本数一数二. 是东京都「难关私大」（非常难考的私立大学）MARCH之一.
1885年7月，增岛六一郎、菊池武夫、穗积陈重、藤田隆三郎等18名青年法律人创立了「英吉利法律学校」. 最初虽然是教授英国法的教育机关，在日本法律相继制定之后也开始教授日本国内法，校名也改名为「东京法学院」、「东京法学院大学」. 而1905年8月因经济学科的设立而改称中央大学. 1920年依正式升格为大学. 也是日本国内历史最悠久的私立大学之一.
中央大学向法律界、官界、财界、政界以及新闻界送出了大量毕业生. 而大学附设的经理研究所横跨学部提供会计学教育. 今日的中央大学是拥有六学部、七研究科及三个专门职研究所，毕业生人数五十万以上的综合大学.
英吉利法律学校的建学精神是「培养实地应用的素质」，以此为基础发展为今日的「个人自由的尊重与实证·合理主义的学风」. 另外，实质刚健被视为学校的校是. 2010年建校125周年之际，启用了'''行动的知性. －Knowledge into Action－'''作为学校的标语.
从最初建立时开始便采取重视实学的理念，现在也重视实习等实际应用的活动. 2003年开始了学部连接项目，为实际应用的学习导入了跨科系的教育. 现在与以欧美、东亚为中心的180间大学签属了派遣交换协定.
en: Chuo University (中央大学), commonly referred to as Chuo (中央) or Chu-Dai (中大), is a private research university in Hachioji, Tokyo, Japan. The university finds its roots in a school called (English Law School), which was founded in 1885, and became a university in 1920. The university operates four campuses in Tokyo: the largest in Hachiōji (Tama campus), one in Bunkyō (Korakuen campus), and two others in Shinjuku (Ichigaya and Ichigaya-Tamachi campuses). Chuo is organized into six faculties, ten graduate schools, and nine research institutes. There are also four affiliated high schools and two affiliated junior high schools.
When written in Chinese characters, Chuo University shares the same name with National Central University in Taiwan and Chung-Ang University in South Korea.

Chuo was founded as the English Law School (英吉利法律学校) in 1885 at Kanda in Tokyo by Rokuichiro Masujima together with some group of 18 young lawyers led by him. Before 1889, the school moved and was renamed to Tokyo College of Law (Tōkyō Hōgakuin). The curriculum was changed to reflect the government reform of Japanese law and creation of a new civil code. Opposition to the implementation of new civil code resulted in the government shuttering of the campus journal and the subsequent creation of the Chuo Law Review (Hōgaku Shinpō), which has been regularly published since then.

The university was burnt down in the Great Kanda Fire that occurred in 1892, but was able to hold temporary classes. Before 1903, the school was promoted to Tokyo University of Law (Tokyo Hōgakuin Daigaku) and in 1905, the school expanded itself with the department of economics and renamed itself Chuo University.

The origin of its name "Chuo" has not been certain. However, many founders of the university were once students of the Middle Temple, London, United Kingdom before they completed their training and became qualified as Barristers. This is one of the reasons why the university was renamed to "Chuo", which literally means middle, center or central.
